original_question: Does there exist a root-finding method, for instance among generalizations of Newton, Konig, or Chebyshev type methods, whose Fatou set contains a Herman ring?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Conclusion, item 7 (open problem), motivated by the discussion in Section 4.3, "Root-finding algorithms and Herman rings."
correct_elements: Your draft captures the paper’s actual open problem very closely: it asks about the existence of a root-finding method whose Fatou set contains a Herman ring, and it mentions the same surrounding families discussed in the paper. In Section 4.3, Newton’s method is treated as the basic benchmark, while König’s and Chebyshev’s methods are singled out as unresolved cases; Section 6 then abstracts this into the broader open question.
missing_details: The paper’s scope is root-finding methods for complex polynomials that produce rational maps under iteration, not arbitrary rational or meromorphic maps.

The existential quantifier is over both the method and an input polynomial: the intended question is whether there exists some root-finding method and some polynomial for which the associated rational map has a Herman ring.
The official formulation is broader than the examples Newton/König/Chebyshev: those are motivating instances from Section 4.3, not a restriction built into the open problem itself.
For stand-alone clarity, the Fatou set should be identified as the Fatou set of the induced rational map obtained from the chosen polynomial and root-finding method.

For stand-alone clarity, a Herman ring should be identified as a periodic doubly connected Fatou component on which a suitable iterate is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of an annulus.
The paper does not impose any extra degree restriction in this open problem, so the refined question should not add one.
refined_question: Does there exist an iterative root-finding method for complex polynomials—i.e. a scheme that assigns to each complex polynomial p a rational map T_p whose roots are attracting fixed points—such that for at least one polynomial p, the Fatou set F(T_p) contains a Herman ring, that is, a periodic doubly connected Fatou component on which an iterate of T_p is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of an annulus?
justification: The draft is aiming at the open problem stated explicitly in Section 6, item 7. Section 4.3 provides the exact local context: Newton maps of polynomials are known not to have Herman rings; for König’s method and Chebyshev’s method the existence of Herman rings is still unknown; and the authors then summarize the state of the subject by saying that no root-finding method is currently known whose Fatou set contains a Herman ring. The conclusion restates this as the official open question. Section 1 supplies the paper’s meanings of Fatou set and Herman ring, so those definitions should be folded into the refined stand-alone version.
